lesson_title: R160 of Beads Became R600 of Bracelets
hook_text: She spent R160 on beads and turned them into R600. Here is how manufacturing works.
clip_script: Naledi's costs for 20 bracelets: beads and wire R160, her own time R100, bags and taxi R40. Total R300. Divide by 20: R15 a bracelet. That is the cost per unit. Similar bracelets sell for R25 to R35, but hers can spell your name. So she charges R30. R15 profit each, R300 for the batch. R160 of beads became R600 of bracelets. That extra is value added: her skill, time and design. That is manufacturing. Trading buys and resells. Manufacturing makes something new. Either way, know your costs.
visual_style: A whiteboard pile of beads transforming into bracelets on a stand, with a cost breakdown and a price tag.
mood: Creative and proud, a maker's story.
pacing: A quick cost build, a market check, then a satisfying value reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work out the cost per unit of something you could make.
